mainEntity.name: How do I convert my annual salary to an hourly wage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multiply your hourly rate by hours per week, then by weeks per year. At $25 an hour, working 40 hours a week across 52 paid weeks gives $52,000 a year. Change the hours or paid weeks to match the pay offer you are comparing.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert hourly pay to an annual salary?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 40-hour week across 52 weeks gives 2,080 work hours. That figure comes from multiplying the weekly hours by the weeks worked, so it changes with your schedule. For example, 37.5 hours a week across 52 weeks gives 1,950 hours.

mainEntity.name: How many hours are in a work year?

acceptedAnswer.text: The salary calculator converts monthly and every-two-weeks amounts using the annual pay implied by your input. Monthly pay is annual pay divided by 12. For the $60,000 single-filer example, the result is $50,390 a year and $1,938.08 across 26 biweekly checks. You can enter gross pay by year or by paycheck. The schedule choices are weekly, every two weeks, twice a month and monthly, with 52, 26, 24 and 12 checks respectively. If you need to convert a pay figure before entering it, use the salary calculator . Federal income tax starts with taxable income: gross pay minus your annual pre-tax retirement contribution and the standard deduction, with a floor of zero. The calculator applies the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) 2026 brackets band by band to that amount. For a single filer earning $60,000, taxable income is $43,900. The first $12,400 is taxed at 10%, producing $1,240. The remaining $31,500 is taxed at 12%, producing $3,780. Those bands add up to $5,020 in federal income tax. Being in a higher bracket does not apply that bracket's rate to every dollar of taxable income. Social Security is 6.2% of gross wages up to the $184,500 wage base. Medicare is 1.45% of all gross wages, and employers withhold an additional 0.9% on wages above $200,000 in a calendar year. Neither tax shrinks when you make a pre-tax retirement contribution. For example, Social Security on a $300,000 salary stops at $11,439, while Medicare comes to $5,250. On $250,000, Medicare is $4,075, which includes $450 in Additional Medicare withholding. The calculator shows Social Security and Medicare separately. A pre-tax retirement contribution lowers the income used to calculate federal income tax, but it does not lower the gross wages used for Social Security or Medicare. On a $100,000 single-filer salary, a $10,000 contribution reduces federal income tax from $13,170 to $10,970. Social Security stays at $6,200, and Medicare stays at $1,450. Annual take-home pay is $71,380 with the contribution, compared with $79,180 without it. The contribution lowers take-home pay by $7,800 because federal income tax falls by $2,200. Enter the contribution as an annual amount, even if you enter gross pay per paycheck. 2026 Federal Figures Used The paycheck calculator uses the following 2026 standard deductions, income tax brackets and payroll tax figures.
